section.title: org.osgi.resource
section.para: Resource Package Version 1.0.
Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. For example:

listitem.para: Capability - A capability that has been declared from a Resource.
Namespace - Capability and Requirement Namespaces base class.
Requirement - A requirement that has been declared from a Resource .
Resource - A resource is the representation of a uniquely identified and typed data.
Wire - A wire connecting a Capability to a Requirement.
Wiring - A wiring for a resource.

section.title: public interface Capability
section.para: A capability that has been declared from a Resource.
Instances of this type must be effectively immutable. That is, for a given instance of this interface, the methods defined by this interface must always return the same result.

formalpara.title: Concurrency
formalpara.para: Thread-safe

section.title: public boolean equals(Object obj)

formalpara.title: obj
formalpara.para: The object to compare against this Capability.

section.para: Compares this Capability to another Capability.
This Capability is equal to another Capability if they have the same namespace, directives and attributes and are declared by the same resource.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: true if this Capability is equal to the other object; false otherwise.

section.para: Returns the attributes of this capability.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: An unmodifiable map of attribute names to attribute values for this capability, or an empty map if this capability has no attributes.

section.title: public Map<String, String> getDirectives()
section.para: Returns the directives of this capability.

formalpara.title: Returns

section.para: Returns the namespace of this capability.

formalpara.para: The namespace of this capability.

section.title: public abstract class Namespace
section.para: Capability and Requirement Namespaces base class.
This class is the common class shared by all OSGi defined namespaces. It defines the names for the common attributes and directives for the OSGi specified namespaces.
The OSGi Alliance reserves the right to extend the set of directives and attributes which have specified semantics for all of the specified namespaces.
The values associated with these keys are of type String, unless otherwise indicated.

formalpara.title: Concurrency
formalpara.para: Immutable

section.title: public static final String CAPABILITY_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE = "effective"
section.para: The capability directive used to specify the effective time for the capability. The default value is resolve.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: resolve, active

section.title: public static final String CAPABILITY_USES_DIRECTIVE = "uses"
section.para: The capability directive used to specify the comma separated list of package names used by a capability.

section.title: public static final String CARDINALITY_MULTIPLE = "multiple"
section.para: The directive value identifying a multiple cardinality type.

section.title: public static final String CARDINALITY_SINGLE = "single"
section.para: The directive value identifying a cardinality type of single.

section.title: public static final String EFFECTIVE_ACTIVE = "active"
section.para: The directive value identifying a capability or requirement that is effective at active time. Capabilities and requirements with an effective time of active are ignored while resolving a resource.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: REQUIREMENT_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE, CAPABILITY_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE

section.title: public static final String EFFECTIVE_RESOLVE = "resolve"
section.para: The directive value identifying a capability or requirement that is effective at resolve time. Capabilities and requirements with an effective time of resolve are the only capabilities which are processed while resolving a resource.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: REQUIREMENT_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE, CAPABILITY_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE

section.title: public static final String REQUIREMENT_CARDINALITY_DIRECTIVE = "cardinality"
section.para: The requirement directive used to specify the cardinality for a requirement. The default value is single.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: multiple, single

section.title: public static final String REQUIREMENT_EFFECTIVE_DIRECTIVE = "effective"
section.para: The requirement directive used to specify the effective time for the requirement. The default value is resolve.

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: resolve, active

section.title: public static final String REQUIREMENT_FILTER_DIRECTIVE = "filter"
section.para: The requirement directive used to specify a capability filter. This filter is used to match against a capability's attributes.

section.title: public static final String REQUIREMENT_RESOLUTION_DIRECTIVE = "resolution"
section.para: The requirement directive used to specify the resolution type for a requirement. The default value is mandatory .

formalpara.title: See Also
formalpara.para: mandatory, optional

section.title: public static final String RESOLUTION_MANDATORY = "mandatory"
section.para: The directive value identifying a mandatory requirement resolution type. A mandatory resolution type indicates that the requirement must be resolved when the resource is resolved. If such a requirement cannot be resolved, the resource fails to resolve.

section.title: public static final String RESOLUTION_OPTIONAL = "optional"
section.para: The directive value identifying an optional requirement resolution type. An optional resolution type indicates that the requirement is optional and the resource may be resolved without the requirement being resolved.

Instances of this type must be effectively immutable. That is, for a given instance of this interface, the methods defined by this interface must always return the same result.

formalpara.title: Concurrency

section.para: Compares this Requirement to another Requirement.
This Requirement is equal to another Requirement if they have the same namespace, directives and attributes and are declared by the same resource.

Requirement attributes have no specified semantics and are considered extra user defined information.

formalpara.para: An unmodifiable map of directive names to directive values for this requirement, or an empty map if this requirement has no directives.

section.title: public String getNamespace()
section.para: Returns the namespace of this requirement.

formalpara.para: The namespace of this requirement.

section.para: Returns the resource declaring this requirement.

formalpara.title: Returns

section.title: public int hashCode()
section.para: Returns the hashCode of this Requirement.

section.title: public interface Resource
section.para: A resource is the representation of a uniquely identified and typed data. A resource declares requirements that need to be satisfied by capabilities before it can provide its capabilities.
Instances of this type must be effectively immutable. That is, for a given instance of this interface, the methods defined by this interface must always return the same result.

formalpara.title: Concurrency
formalpara.para: Thread-safe

section.title: public boolean equals(Object obj)

formalpara.title: obj
formalpara.para: The object to compare against this Resource.

section.para: Compares this Resource to another Resource.

This Resource is equal to another Resource if both have the same content and come from the same location. Location may be defined as the bundle location if the resource is an installed bundle or the repository location if the resource is in a repository.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: true if this Resource is equal to the other object; false otherwise.

section.title: public List<Capability> getCapabilities(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the declared capabilities to return or null to return the declared capabilities from all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the capabilities declared by this resource.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: An unmodifiable list containing the declared Capabilitys from the specified namespace. The returned list will be empty if this resource declares no capabilities in the specified namespace.

section.title: public List<Requirement> getRequirements(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the declared requirements to return or null to return the declared requirements from all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the requirements declared by this bundle resource.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: An unmodifiable list containing the declared Requirement s from the specified namespace. The returned list will be empty if this resource declares no requirements in the specified namespace.

section.title: public int hashCode()
section.para: Returns the hashCode of this Resource.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The hashCode of this Resource.

formalpara.title: Concurrency

The returned resource may differ from the resource referenced by the requirement.

formalpara.title: Returns

section.para: Returns the hashCode of this Wire.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The hashCode of this Wire.

section.title: public interface Wiring
section.para: A wiring for a resource. A wiring is associated with a resource and represents the dependencies with other wirings.
Instances of this type must be effectively immutable. That is, for a given instance of this interface, the methods defined by this interface must always return the same result.

formalpara.title: Concurrency
formalpara.para: Thread-safe

section.title: public List<Wire> getProvidedResourceWires(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the capabilities for which to return wires or null to return the wires for the capabilities in all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the Wires to the provided capabilities of this wiring.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: A list containing a snapshot of the Wires for the capabilities of this wiring, or an empty list if this wiring has no capabilities in the specified namespace. For a given namespace, the list contains the wires in the order the capabilities were specified in the manifests of the resource and the attached fragment resources of this wiring. There is no ordering defined between capabilities in different namespaces.

section.title: public List<Wire> getRequiredResourceWires(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the requirements for which to return wires or null to return the wires for the requirements in all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the Wires to the requirements in use by this wiring.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: A list containing a snapshot of the Wires for the requirements of this wiring, or an empty list if this wiring has no requirements in the specified namespace. For a given namespace, the list contains the wires in the order the requirements were specified in the manifests of the resource and the attached fragment resources of this wiring. There is no ordering defined between requirements in different namespaces.

section.title: public Resource getResource()
section.para: Returns the resource associated with this wiring.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The resource associated with this wiring.

section.title: public List<Capability> getResourceCapabilities(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the capabilities to return or null to return the capabilities from all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the capabilities provided by this wiring.
Only capabilities considered by the resolver are returned. For example, capabilities with effective directive not equal to resolve are not returned.
A capability may not be required by any wiring and thus there may be no wires for the capability.

A wiring for a non-fragment resource provides a subset of the declared capabilities from the resource and all attached fragment resources†. Not all declared capabilities may be provided since some may be discarded. For example, if a package is declared to be both exported and imported, only one is selected and the other is discarded.
A wiring for a fragment resource with a symbolic name must provide exactly one osgi.identity capability.
† The osgi.identity capability provided by attached fragment resource must not be included in the capabilities of the host wiring.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: A list containing a snapshot of the Capabilitys, or an empty list if this wiring provides no capabilities in the specified namespace. For a given namespace, the list contains the capabilities in the order the capabilities were specified in the manifests of the resource and the attached fragment resources† of this wiring. There is no ordering defined between capabilities in different namespaces.

section.title: public List<Requirement> getResourceRequirements(String namespace)

formalpara.title: namespace
formalpara.para: The namespace of the requirements to return or null to return the requirements from all namespaces.

section.para: Returns the requirements of this wiring.
Only requirements considered by the resolver are returned. For example, requirements with effective directive not equal to resolve are not returned.

A wiring for a non-fragment resource has a subset of the declared requirements from the resource and all attached fragment resources. Not all declared requirements may be present since some may be discarded. For example, if a package is declared to be both exported and imported, only one is selected and the other is discarded.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: A list containing a snapshot of the Requirements, or an empty list if this wiring uses no requirements in the specified namespace. For a given namespace, the list contains the requirements in the order the requirements were specified in the manifests of the resource and the attached fragment resources of this wiring. There is no ordering defined between requirements in different namespaces.
